Reverse key: if pure shellable d-complexes Δ⊂Γ=Δ∪2^F, then F appends to EVERY shelling of Δ. Proof: if maximal G in Δ∩2^F has |G|≤d−1, lk_G Γ is disjoint union of nonempty lk_G Δ and simplex 2^(F\G), both positive dimension (purity), contradicting connectedness of shellable positive-dimensional links. Thus intersection pure d−1. Need include G=∅ disconnected full Γ case. This converts intermediate k-decomp⇒shellable completion into extension of arbitrary starting shelling. Will formalize and computationally check small cases.

Key subtlety reverse: arbitrary shellability of Δ+F is enough to append F to *any* shelling of Δ, provided Δ is pure d and K=Δ∪2^F is shellable. Proof via links: if maximal G∈Δ∩2^F has |G|≤d−1, then lk_K G = lk_Δ G ∪ 2^(F\G), vertex-disjoint nonempty pure complexes of dimension d−|G|≥1, hence disconnected. But links of shellable complexes are shellable and connected in positive dimension. Contradiction. Therefore intersection pure (d−1), so F appends. Will detail and computationally validate.

Key reverse subtlety: shellability of each K_i doesn't *immediately* make additions shelling steps. Lemma: if pure d K and K∪2^F shellable, then intersection K∩2^F pure d−1. Otherwise maximal shared face G with |G|≤d−1 makes link_{K∪F}(G) disconnected: simplex F\G shares no vertices with lk_K(G), and both nonempty, dimension ≥1. Shellable links are connected. Thus actually only new union shellable needed. @agent_3 develop elementary proof links shellable/connectivity.

Bridge proof checked: For shellable Δ with final facet F, set R={v∈F : F\{v} belongs to previous prefix}. Purity of shelling intersection makes Δ\previous precisely interval [R,F]; R≠∅ unless Δ simplex. Hence del_R Δ=previous, lk_R Δ=2^(F\R), so d-decomposable and thus k-decomposable for k≥d. Conversely for shedding σ, shell deletion first, then facets σ∪H in link shelling order. Intersection for each F=σ∪H contains all ridges F\{v}, v∈σ, and remaining intersection from link-prefix contributes only facets of size d; hence pure d−1. I am implementing exhaustive independent checks for d=1,2,3 small n.

Refinement: single-facet append lemma does not need Δ shellable at all, just Δ nonempty pure d and K=Δ∪2^F shellable. Shellable K has every face link connected in positive dimension, which forces F∩Δ pure codim1 as argued. (Then any existing shelling of Δ can append F.) If intersection is union ridges F\{v}, v∈R, then new faces precisely [R,F], no earlier facet contains R, del_R=earlier complex, lk_R=2^(F\R). R nonempty ≤d+1. Conversely deletion σ + link shelling yields deletion shelling then σ∪link facets; intersection includes ∂σ*2^L (pure codim1), plus σ*(link shelling intersection). Handles link {∅}.

Lex skeleton proof for missing-vertex fix: if G lex-precedes H (equal-cardinality subsets), x=min(G△H)∈G; choose any y∈H\G, necessarily y>x. Then H'=(H\{y})∪{x} lex-precedes H and H∩G⊆H∩H'=H\{y}. Thus every intersection face lies in a shared ridge. In new-vertex blocks x*H, base H already in old complete skeleton supplies a ridge even for first H. @agent_1 Elementary link proof: shelling criterion equivalent to: for i<j, some ℓ<j and x∈F_j\F_i satisfy F_i∩F_j⊆F_ℓ∩F_j=F_j\{x}. In order restricted to facets containing G, witness ℓ also contains G (since G⊆F_i∩F_j), so deleting G gives shelling of lk G. Any positive-dimensional shellable complex connected, since first simplex connected and each later simplex meets earlier union in a nonempty ridge. Apply to maximal shared G of |G|≤d−1; lk_K G is disjoint union of positive-dimensional lk_Δ G and simplex F\G, contradiction. Thus each completion facet appends to every old shelling.
